source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Secure Boot feature is Active if Secure Boot is Enabled, Platform Key (PK) is enrolled and the System is in User mode. The mode change requires platform reset [Enable/Disable]
1. In CSM configuration, set all item to UEFI and disable CSM.
2. Enable secure boot with build-in factory key loaded.
3. Install OS via any media.
4. Disable secure boot(unsigned OS) with below command:\
     "sudo update-secureboot-policy" \
     Follow insctrction to disable secure boot.
5. Reboot system, press any key when you see the MOK management
6. Select Change Secure Boot state,than enter passowrd you set in step4 as request.
7. Boot should fail with unsigned OS.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. System could boot to BIOS after setting
2. System able to boot with signed OS when secure boot is enable.
3. System cannot be boot with unsigned OS when secure boot is enable.

original_method: After correction, establish UEFI-only/CSM-disabled mode and factory keys, prove signed-OS boot under enabled Secure Boot, execute the explicitly defined unsigned artifact in the intended state, capture firmware/OS/MOK state at each transition, and restore the approved baseline.
manual_activity: After correction, BIOS CSM/key changes, MOK interaction and direct boot-result observation require a human; the agent may collect state/evidence but cannot resolve the contradictory state transition.

Target disk/backup or approved non-destructive boot media

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: mokutil --sb-state is useful readback; a ten-line dmesg excerpt is incomplete and neither command proves signed boot or unsigned rejection. update-secureboot-policy is preserved but prohibited until its intended effect is clarified.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not introduce a substitute command. After correction, retain full mokutil/key-state and boot evidence using the project-approved OS/version-specific method.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: UEFI-only/CSM-disabled, built-in factory key, OS installation, update-secureboot-policy/MOK steps, signed/unsigned criteria and 60/90-minute fields are preserved pending correction.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define separate signed and unsigned artifacts and a state table for CSM, Setup/User mode, PK/KEK/db, MOK and Secure Boot before each boot attempt; collect exact hashes and boot-chain evidence.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact firmware and OS Secure Boot implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS, shim, mokutil, kernel and OS media versions.

modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A MOK policy change is not equivalent to disabling firmware Secure Boot on every OS/platform.

project_override_considerations: A project supplies media, disk strategy, key policy and allowed state transitions, but cannot silently reinterpret the master conflict. A case-specific owner ruling must identify the intended unsigned-boot state and MOK behavior.
expected_evidence: Owner correction and approved state matrix
Platform/firmware/OS identity and baseline CSM/key/MOK state
Signed artifact hash and successful boot evidence in the approved enabled state
Unsigned artifact hash and rejection evidence in the explicitly approved state
Full mokutil/firmware/console evidence plus restored final state
Engineer verdict separated from tool results

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Step 4 says to disable Secure Boot and steps 5-6 complete a MOK state change, while step 7 and Criteria require an unsigned OS to fail when Secure Boot is enabled. These states imply opposite expected behavior and cannot both define one boot attempt.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The security state at the decisive unsigned-OS attempt is undefined by contradictory source instructions. Executing either interpretation would alter coverage and may make the system unbootable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its readback only as supporting evidence and restores the boot matrix, key state and conflict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with the genuine SOURCE_CONFLICT/BLOCKED conclusion and preserves its recovery controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Records a scoped engineering decision while separating execution readiness, tool evidence and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents a simple enabled-state query from being reported as signed/unsigned boot validation and stops contradictory key/MOK changes before an approved recovery plan exists.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unsigned-boot rejection is meaningful only with an explicit, verified Secure Boot/key state. Because the source tells the operator both to disable the mechanism and expect enabled-state rejection, the core acceptance semantics are genuinely unresolved and BLOCKED.
no_automatic_retry: Do not alter or retry any key, MOK, CSM, OS-install or boot step before resolution; afterward preserve the first failure and obtain engineer disposition.
